andino.name: Andino

connections.label: PWM output — duty-limited, not a fixed rail
power (rail not specified in the data)

wiring.note: Andino's documented build, wired the standard way: the battery bus feeds the L298N driver (parts-catalog max 35 V in) and a 5 V buck converter — the catalog part whose stated job is powering 'the computer and logic from the main battery' — which feeds the Raspberry Pi 4 at 5 V. The Arduino Nano sits between the Pi and the driver and reads the motor encoders. Driver output to the motors is PWM: duty-limited, not a fixed rail, so that connection carries no voltage and is never voltage-checked. Voltages are the spec's battery voltage, the motors' recorded 3-9 V rating (SparkFun, via the official BOM) and catalog datasheet values; anything unsourced is 'not specified'. Harness-check data (2026-10-27): the buck converter's 5 A rated output is the parts catalog's record for that part; the L298N's 4 A total rated output and 5 V TTL logic are from the ST L298 datasheet; the Nano's 5 V TTL serial is from the Arduino Nano datasheet; the Pi 4's 3.3 V GPIO logic is from the Raspberry Pi documentation; the RPLIDAR A1M8's 3.3 V TTL UART and 0.4 A typical work-mode draw (300 mA scanner + 100 mA motor at 5 V) are from the SLAMTEC A1M8 datasheet. The Pi-to-Nano serial link therefore crosses 3.3 V and 5 V logic with no level shifter recorded — the harness checks flag it, as they should.

andino.physics_reason: Andino's official model ships as xacro (andino.urdf.xacro plus included files) — a format a build tool must expand before anything can parse it. No plain URDF is recorded for this entry, so there is nothing honest to run the checks on.

The Pi is the 'Pi' in Waffle Pi; its 5 V requirement is the Raspberry Pi supply spec in the parts catalog. Harness-check data (2026-10-27): the Dynamixel bus logic level (5 V TTL) is ROBOTIS's published figure for the XL430 (e-Manual: 'TTL Multidrop Bus (5V Logic)'), the Pi's GPIO logic is 3.3 V per the Raspberry Pi documentation, and the bus cables terminate in the same Robot Cable-X3P plug at both ends (ROBOTIS cable table). nodes.req_label: documented input range 10.0–14.8 V; stall torque 3.8 N·m at 11.1 V

wiring.note: The OP3's documented pattern: the battery powers the OpenCR sub-controller, and the OpenCR distributes power and data to all twenty XM430-W350 servos over the daisy-chained Dynamixel TTL bus. The servos' documented input range is 10.0–14.8 V (rated_max_v records the 11.1 V bus voltage this robot actually runs). The Intel NUC's own power feed is not part of the documented bus and is not shown. Harness-check data (2026-10-27): the OpenCR's 12 V output is rated at 4.5 A maximum in the ROBOTIS OpenCR e-Manual, and the bus cables terminate in the same Robot Cable-X3P plug at both ends (ROBOTIS cable table, as recorded for the cable above). No logic level is recorded for the bus: the OP3's servos are the RS-485 variant (XM430-W350-R), and RS-485 is a differential bus, not a 3.3/5 V logic family. Servo load currents stay unrecorded — ROBOTIS publishes stall current only, a peak its manual says is not a continuous rating.

robotis-op3.physics_reason: The recorded model for the OP3 is an MJCF from the MuJoCo menagerie, not a URDF. The physics checks parse URDF, so they do not run on this entry.
